claims.text: The initial TiVNbTa alloy is a single-phase BCC refractory high-entropy alloy with a dendritic microstructure.
The baseline TiVNbTa alloy has a yield strength of 330 MPa at 1273 K.
The baseline TiVNbTa alloy has a compressive strength of 423 MPa at 1273 K and 30% strain.
Adding 1–3 vol% thermally stable ceramic nanoparticles is the proposed intervention.
Y2O3 or TiC can serve as the proposed ceramic nanoparticle phase.
Mechanical alloying followed by spark-plasma sintering or hot pressing can produce a uniform nanoparticle dispersion in the TiVNbTa matrix.
The ceramic nanoparticles will remain uniformly dispersed within the BCC TiVNbTa matrix.
The dispersed nanoparticles will pin dislocations.
The dispersed nanoparticles will pin grain boundaries and impede grain-boundary sliding at elevated temperature.
Impeded dislocation motion and grain-boundary sliding will reduce creep and high-temperature softening.
Nanoparticle dispersion will increase the TiVNbTa yield strength at 1273 K by at least 30% relative to the 330 MPa baseline.
The modified alloy will have a yield strength greater than 430 MPa at 1273 K.
The modified alloy will retain more than 30% strain capability at 1273 K.
The nanoparticle dispersion will improve resistance to microstructural degradation during cycling between room temperature and 1273 K.
The proposed operating envelope includes compression at approximately 10^-3 s^-1 and applied loads up to 500 MPa.
The proposed result is not guaranteed above 1273 K or under loading modes other than compression.
The magnitude of strengthening depends on nanoparticle dispersion quality and volume fraction.
A nonoptimal nanoparticle dispersion may reduce ductility.
